question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

If sodium metal is dropped into water (a)/ it reacts violently (b)/ and had produced hydrogen gas (c)/ along with a large amount of heat. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a zero conditional sentence expressing a general truth or scientific fact, both the if-clause and the main clause must use the simple present tense. Since "reacts" is present tense, "had produced" must also be present tense: "produces".

◦ Corrected sentence: If sodium metal is dropped into water, it reacts violently and produces hydrogen gas, along with a large amount of heat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "If sodium metal is dropped into water" is proper, with the passive present simple "is dropped" describing a general condition.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "it reacts violently" is proper, in the simple present tense.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "along with a large amount of heat" is a proper continuation, with no tense issue.

 

NOTE

 

• If you heat ice, it melted., If you mix red and blue, you got purple. (zero conditional: present simple + present simple, for general truths).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

If the monsoon arrives on schedule this year (a)/ the farmers will sow (b)/ the paddy crop early (c)/ and expected a bountiful harvest by autumn. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a first conditional sentence (if + present simple, ...will + base verb), every verb in the main clause describing the future result must be in the simple future. Since "will sow" is future, "expected" must also be "will expect".

◦ Corrected sentence: If the monsoon arrives on schedule this year, the farmers will sow the paddy crop early and will expect a bountiful harvest by autumn.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "If the monsoon arrives on schedule this year" is proper, with the if-clause in the simple present.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the farmers will sow" is proper, in the simple future.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "the paddy crop early" is a proper object phrase, with no tense issue.

 

NOTE

 

• If it rains tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic and informed everyone. → and will inform everyone (first conditional: every main-clause verb needs "will").

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

If you will submit the loan application before Friday (a)/ the bank will process (b)/ your request within a week (c)/ and notify you immediately after approval. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The if-clause of a first conditional sentence must always be in the simple present tense; "will" should never appear in the if-clause. So "will submit" must be "submit".

◦ Corrected sentence: If you submit the loan application before Friday, the bank will process your request within a week and notify you immediately after approval.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the bank will process" is proper, in the simple future.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "your request within a week" is a proper object phrase.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "and notify you immediately after approval" correctly continues the future main clause.

 

NOTE

 

• If she will call me, I will let you know. → If she calls me (never use "will" in a first-conditional if-clause).

question:

If the committee approves the new bylaw next week, (a)/ every housing society in the district have to comply with it within thirty days, (b)/ failing which penalties will be imposed. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a first conditional main clause, the verb describing the future obligation must agree with the simple future sense already established. Since the sentence describes a future requirement, "have to comply" must be "will have to comply".

◦ Corrected sentence: If the committee approves the new bylaw next week, every housing society in the district will have to comply with it within thirty days, failing which penalties will be imposed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "If the committee approves the new bylaw next week," is proper, with the if-clause in the simple present.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "failing which penalties will be imposed" is a proper future continuation.

 

• Option (d) No error — this is incorrect since an error exists in part (b).

 

NOTE

 

• If the flight is delayed, the airline provide a refund. → the airline will provide (first conditional main clause needs "will").

question:

solution_text:

• In a second conditional sentence, the verb "to be" in the if-clause is always "were", for every subject, including "I". So "was" must be "were".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "I would introduce" is proper, in the second-conditional main clause.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "a mandatory internship programme" is a proper object phrase.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "for every final-year student" correctly completes the sentence.

question:

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a second conditional sentence, every verb in the main clause governed by "if I were you" must use "would" + base verb, not "will". Since "would definitely renegotiate" is used, "will not accept" must also be "would not accept".

◦ Corrected sentence: If I were you, I would definitely renegotiate the terms of that start-up job offer before making any final decision, and would not accept it without a higher signing bonus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "If I were you," is proper, using the fixed subjunctive "were".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "I would definitely renegotiate the terms of that start-up job offer" is proper, using "would + base verb".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "before making any final decision," is a proper adverbial phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• If I were in charge, I will change the policy. → I would change the policy (second conditional main clause always uses "would", not "will").

question:

During the pre-flight inspection, (a)/ if the pilot had noticed the warning light earlier, (b)/ he prevent the technical snag from escalating further (c)/ by alerting the ground crew right away. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a third conditional sentence, the main clause describing the unreal past result must use "could have" + past participle. So "prevent" must be "could have prevented".

◦ Corrected sentence: During the pre-flight inspection, if the pilot had noticed the warning light earlier, he could have prevented the technical snag from escalating further by alerting the ground crew right away.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "During the pre-flight inspection," is a proper adverbial opener.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "if the pilot had noticed the warning light earlier," is proper, in the past perfect.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "by alerting the ground crew right away" is a proper gerund phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• If they had left earlier, they would have reached the station on time and catch their connecting train. → and would have caught (every verb in a third-conditional main clause needs "would/could have + past participle").

question:

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The entire presentation would have been revised well before the meeting (a)/ to address every likely objection, (b)/ especially regarding pricing, (c)/ if I knew that the client would reject the initial proposal. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a third conditional if-clause, the verb must be in the past perfect, not the simple past. So "knew" must be "had known".

◦ Corrected sentence: The entire presentation would have been revised well before the meeting to address every likely objection, especially regarding pricing, if I had known that the client would reject the initial proposal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The entire presentation would have been revised well before the meeting" is proper, using "would have been + past participle".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "to address every likely objection," is a proper purpose phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "especially regarding pricing," is a proper continuation.

 

NOTE

 

• We would have booked earlier if we knew about the fare hike. → if we had known (third conditional if-clause needs past perfect, not simple past).
